newsitem.title: USA: Ford said mulling North American plant closures.
newsitem.headline: Ford said mulling North American plant closures.

text.p: Ford Motor Co is considering possible assembly plant closures in North America as a means to boost the profitability of its core operations, an industry source said on Thursday.
Ford's Lorain, Ohio, car plant, which now builds the slow selling Ford Thunderbird and Mercury Cougar mid-size coupes, may be closed in the next several years, the source said.

"The latest plan at Ford from people I've been talking to is that they will shut Lorain car," the source said. "The sport/utility (vehicle) they were going to build there, they will do at St. Louis instead."
Ford Automotive Group President Jacques Nasser said the company has no plans to close any plants, although he said the company constantly studies alternatives for its manufacturing facilities.
"But we have no plans and we've made no decisions on plant closings," he said.
The plant closing issue was first reported Thursday by the Wall Street Journal, in a story that Nasser said was "surprising and lacking substance."
